items.title: Enugu Govt denies role in attack on NDC members
items.description: Government blames airport clash on lack of FAAN approval, says police probe secretariat incident By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — The Enugu State Government has denied involvement in Saturday’s incidents involving members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport and the party’s state secretariat in Enugu, alleging that the airport confrontation arose from the party’s attempt to hold a rally without the necessary approval. The government also dismissed reports that the secretariat incident claimed a life, saying one party member, identified as Ifeanyi Nworie, sustained gunshot injuries and was receiving medical attention. The Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Chidiebere Ọnyia, stated the government’s position while addressing journalists at the Government House, Enugu. Ọnyia said the government had investigated the circumstances surrounding the incidents after reports allegedly linked it to the attacks. “The attention of the Enugu State Government has been drawn to the false reports associating it with the Saturday, October 10, 2026 incidents involving the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport (AIIA) and the party’s Enugu State Office at GRA, Enugu,” he said. According to him, the airport incident was a matter between the NDC and federal authorities, but the state government made inquiries to establish what happened. He said the NDC had published a notice inviting members and supporters to what it described as its “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the airport. The notice was also reportedly published on the Facebook page of the party’s governorship candidate in the state. Ọnyia said the police had advised the party to obtain approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) before security personnel could be deployed to the airport for the event. He alleged that the party proceeded without securing the required approval. “Further findings, however, revealed that the NDC did not secure the approval of FAAN to host a grand statewide rally at its facility. Security agencies, therefore, advised the organisers of the rally to rethink it,” he said. According to the SSG, the party nevertheless mobilised its members to the airport, where an attempt to gain entry into the facility resulted in a confrontation with airport authorities. He said security agencies intervened and dispersed the party members to restore order around the airport, which he described as a strategic national asset. Ọnyia said the government’s account was consistent with the statement issued by the Enugu State Police Command on Sunday, October 11. Police investigating secretariat clash On the incident at the NDC state secretariat, the SSG said security reports indicated that a violent clash had occurred and that the police were investigating the matter. He identified the injured party member as Ifeanyi Nworie, 43, who allegedly sustained a gunshot wound and was taken to the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Park Lane, before being transferred to the National Orthopaedic Hospital, Enugu, for further treatment. “We can, therefore, authoritatively report that there were no deaths as falsely claimed by some reports and NDC leaders,” Ọnyia said. The government condemned political violence and maintained that Governor Peter Mbah’s administration was committed to protecting residents irrespective of their political affiliations. Ọnyia said the administration’s security investments were intended to sustain peace and create an environment conducive to business, investment and tourism. He also called on political parties and politicians to embrace peaceful campaigns and issue-based engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections. Government accuses opposition of political mischief The SSG questioned the decision to plan a statewide campaign flag-off at the airport without the approval of the relevant authorities. He also disputed allegations that the governor’s Chief Security Officer was present at the NDC secretariat and supervised the shooting. According to Ọnyia, the security officer was with Governor Mbah at the Teachers Grassroots Movement rally at Okpara Square, Enugu, at the time of the incident. He further criticised the opposition for reportedly observing a minute’s silence for a person the government said was alive, describing the action as an attempt to mislead the public. The government also accused opposition parties in the state of trying to create the impression that Enugu was unsafe and that the administration was intolerant of dissent. These claims were made by the government and were not independently established in the statement. Ọnyia alleged that the government had uncovered plots by some opposition elements to engage armed thugs and bandits to create panic and insecurity ahead of the 2027 elections. He did not provide details of the alleged plots in the statement. The government reiterated its commitment to citizens’ democratic rights, including freedom of association, peaceful assembly, campaigning and voting for candidates of their choice. It said the right of Enugu residents to elect their leaders through free, fair and credible elections remained central to the democratic process. The post Enugu Govt denies role in attack on NDC members appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Présidentielle en France : Raphaël Glucksmann remporte la primaire de la gauche non mélenchoniste
items.description: a l'issue d'un vote sans suspens, mais dont le resultat fait la une de la presse francaise ce 11 octobre, Raphael Glucksmann a remporte la primaire dite « sociale-democrate » avec 66,13% des suffrages, loin devant Olivier Faure et ses 14,46%. Sur la derniere marche du podium figure Segolene Royal, qui a obtenu 7,62% des suffrages, suivie de Emmanuel Maurel avec 5,92% des votes puis de Jerome Guedj avec 5,83%. Le copresident de Place publique etait donne gagnant , credite de 33 % des intentions de vote, par un sondage Harris Interactive publie le 9 octobre, jour d'ouverture de cette primaire qui a ete prolonge jusqu'a ce 11 octobre apres l'annonce d'une cyberattaque contre la plateforme de vote. En tout, 140 000 personnes s'etaient inscrites pour voter a cette primaire, bien loin des 2,8 millions de votants lors de la primaire de 2012 qui avait mis en lice Francois Hollande. Francois Hollande en embuscade ? Reste a savoir comment performera Raphael Glucksmann face a l'autre candidat de la gauche : le leader de La France insoumise Jean-Luc Melenchon. Jusqu'a present donne perdant – dans la plupart des sondages – face au dernier tribun de la vie politique francaise, Raphael Glucksmann affirmait debut juin qu'il « plie[rait] » Melenchon dans un match a gauche au premier tour. Une affirmation d'autant plus piquante que le charisme du candidat social-democrate est objet de railleries en France. Railleries qui viennent tant de ses opposants politiques, a l'instar du president des Republicains Bruno Retailleau, selon lequel Raphael Glucksmann aurait « le charisme d'un horodateur en panne », que de son propre camp : « Le gars qui pretend tenir tete a Poutine, il a ses antiseches sur son portable », taclait ainsi Segolene Royal. Raphael Glucksmann pourrait neanmoins avoir a composer avec une « inconnue », selon une partie de la presse francaise : Francois Hollande et ses velleites de retour a l'elysee. Celui-ci « parie sur un effondrement de Raphael Glucksmann d'ici au mois de janvier pour apparaître comme une solution de recours », peut-on ainsi lire. Reste a savoir si celui-ci voudra vraiment etre celui qui ecopera de l'ardoise budgetaire et sociale des deux quinquennats Macron.

items.title: Fazl accuses govt of reneging on its commitments after seeking his mediation with PTI
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman — who was being cast as the man who could defuse tensions between the Centre and the PTI until Sunday — has accused the government of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts for mediating between the two parties. Both sides held separate meetings with Fazl ahead of their political tensions culminating into the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where the PTI was in power. Addressing a press conference on Sunday, Fazl shared details of his engagement with both sides at a press conference held at his residence in Islamabad following an emergency meeting of the party’s Central Core Committee. He said he returned from Umrah on Oct 7, after which opposition leaders approached him and asked him to play a role in resolving the political impasse. The following day, he continued, federal ministers also visited him and sought his intervention. Tensions between the two sides had risen since the PTI announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. An impasse had emerged after talks between the two sides failed to yield any positive outcomes last week, following which the PTI began its march but remained within KP. Meanwhile, several federal ministers spoke about the possibility of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, linking it with the province’s security situation and the PTI’s alleged non-cooperation on counterterrorism. At the press conference on Sunday, Fazl said the PTI’s march had avoided entering Islamabad at his request and the government’s plan to impose emergency was deferred after its delegation approached him. “Subsequently, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif invited me to the Prime Minister House for a meeting. Although I felt the government had already made up its mind, my colleagues advised me to meet the prime minister,” he said. He said the government had insisted that the long march be called off first while the PTI demanded that its leaders be allowed to meet Imran in jail and court order regarding his transfer to a private hospital be implemented. Both sides were insisting that the other should take the first step, Fazl recalled. “I asked both sides to authorise me to act as a mediator and make decisions to move the process forward,” he said, adding that he also wanted to take now dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi into confidence. He said he held a conference call with Afridi, PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI leader Asad Qaiser, among others. Fazl said that during the conversation, he asked the KP chief minister whether the PTI was willing to end its long march if its demands were accepted. “Sohail Afridi said that if the demands were accepted, they would call off the long march.” Fazl said he had also visited the Prime Minister House and informed him that the PTI was ready to end its march if its demands were met. “I asked the prime minister to give an assurance that the PTI would be allowed to meet Imran Khan, and Imran Khan will receive the required medical treatment,” he said. The JUI-F chief said also intended to travel to Peshawar to hold further discussions with Afridi and other stakeholders, and that he wanted to involve two representatives each from the PTI and the PML-N in the negotiations under his “supervision to advance the process”. However, he said, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called him during the cabinet meeting on Sunday and informed him that the government wanted to impose an emergency in KP because of the security situation. “I questioned the rationale behind the proposed measure, pointing out that the security situation in Balochistan was worse than in KP, yet the government had not imposed governor’s rule there.” Fazl then accused the government of reneging on its commitments despite agreeing to a proposed course of action, saying he had questioned Dar about the purpose of seeking his mediation if the cabinet intended to make its own decision. “I asked Dar why I was asked to mediate if the cabinet was going to make the decision on its own,” he said. Asked whether politicians were responsible for the failure of negotiations, the JUI-F chief said the question should be put to the prime minister. “Ask Shehbaz Sharif how much authority he had during the negotiations,” he said. He further alleged that the government had created obstacles in the way of negotiations. ‘Attack on democracy’ Fazl also rejected the government’s move to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, terming it an “attack on democracy and the rights of the people”. “We reject the entire decision, word for word,” he said. The JUI-F chief said his party would challenge the decision through all available democratic and constitutional forums, including Parliament and the courts. “We will defend the Constitution, human rights and democratic rights in this country through constitutional and democratic platforms available to us,” he said. “We are not prepared to bow, even for a moment, before such unconstitutional measures.” He also regretted the PPP’s role in matter, describing it as one that undermined the Constitution and democracy. Reiterating that “we stand firmly with the Constitution of Pakistan”, he went on to refer to military operations over the year, beginning from the tenure of former military ruler retired General Pervez Musharraf to the present day. This strategy had repeatedly failed, he said. Responding to a question about the provincial government’s performance in KP, Fazl said that if the KP government had failed, the situation in Balochistan was worse. Asked if the opposition would resign from the assemblies, Fazl said the decision would be considered when the situation arose.

items.title: Child marriage robs girls of their future — First Lady
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu has called for an end to child marriage in Nigeria, warning that no girl should be denied education, safety, health or the right to determine her own future. In a message marking the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child, observed on Sunday, October 11, Tinubu said the country must move beyond rhetoric and take decisive action against a practice that cuts short girls’ childhood and limits national progress. The 2026 global commemoration is anchored on the theme, “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights,” which spotlights child marriage as one of the most urgent barriers to girls’ education, health, safety and leadership. The First Lady said girls everywhere deserve to grow up free from discrimination, violence and harmful traditional practices. “Every girl deserves the freedom to learn, grow, and pursue her dreams without discrimination, violence or harmful practices limiting her future,” Mrs. Tinubu said. She described girls as carriers of “voices, strength, potential, and leadership,” insisting that their rights must be protected not only in law but in homes, schools, communities and public policy. “On the International Day of the Girl 2026, we celebrate the voices, strength, potential, and leadership of girls everywhere,” she said. Placing child marriage at the centre of her message, Tinubu urged families, traditional and community leaders, policymakers and government institutions to confront the practice squarely. “I encourage families, communities, leaders, and policymakers to protect the rights of every girl, end child marriage, and invest in her education, health, and general well-being,” she said. The First Lady argued that protecting girls is not merely a social duty but an economic and developmental imperative. “When girls thrive, families prosper, communities grow stronger and nations advance,” she said. items.title: Amnesty condemns cancellation of Tinubu book presentation
items.description: Rights group alleges political pressure, urges ABU to uphold freedom of expression Amnesty International Nigeria has condemned the cancellation of a planned public presentation of a book critically examining President Bola Tinubu’s administration, describing the decision as an attack on freedom of expression. The organisation disclosed this on its X platform on Sunday, accusing the authorities of Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, of succumbing to political pressure over the planned presentation of the book, Tinubu: From Renewed Hope to Despair: A Critical Examination of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Government. The presentation was scheduled for Thursday, October 15, 2026, at Arewa House, Kaduna. Amnesty International said the organisers, the Centre for Democratic Development Research and Training (CEDDERT), Zaria, encountered difficulties securing an alternative venue after the cancellation. According to the rights group, hotels and event centres approached by the organisers in Kaduna declined to host the event, with some reportedly saying they had been warned against accommodating it. The organisation described the development as part of what it called an escalating pattern of political repression and intolerance of dissenting opinions in Nigeria. It argued that the book, which examines government policies and their implications for Nigerians, constituted a legitimate form of intellectual engagement and posed no threat to public peace. “Everything the book was already in public domain,” the organisation said, arguing that attempts to prevent its presentation could create a climate of fear and make it increasingly difficult for citizens to express dissenting views. Amnesty International called on the authorities to end what it described as attacks on freedom of expression and association. It also urged the authorities of Ahmadu Bello University to uphold freedom of expression and called for the immediate and unconditional reversal of the cancellation of the booking for the presentation at Arewa House, Kaduna. The organisation maintained that the rights to freedom of expression and association must be respected. The post Amnesty condemns cancellation of Tinubu book presentation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Iran says US response to its proposal to reopen Hormuz was 'insufficient'
items.description: DUBAI, Oct 11 (Reuters) - The United States' response to Iran's seven conditions in a proposal to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz was "insufficient", Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, was quoted by state media on Sunday as saying. Iran presented a proposal during the UN General Assembly under which the Strait of Hormuz waterway could be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days if the conditions were met, to which the US later replied via Qatari intermediaries.

items.title: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack
items.description: A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, a day after another attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations at the facility. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war , where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. The group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group “carried out four qualitative operations in the past 24 hours using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones”. Saree said they targeted the Riyadh airport multiple times, as well as the Dammam airport and two facilities belonging to the Saudi state oil company Aramco. Hours later, the Saudi coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire. Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added. The civil aviation authority said the attack caused an unspecified number of injuries, and that a damage assessment was underway. AFP journalists and locals reported hearing the sound of multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday. “The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city. ‘Full-fledged war crime’ The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport — where three people were also killed on Thursday — as well as on other key targets in the world’s top crude oil exporter. And although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through. “Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves against Houthi attacks,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University. The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”. Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday. Saturday’s attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the “horrific terrorist attack”. Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 wounded. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before. A Riyadh-based Western diplomat told AFP the official number of injured may not give a full picture, as it did not appear to include those with minor wounds. Operations suspended Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source said, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 21:00 GMT (2am PKT on Monday). A second aviation source confirmed the halt in operations “until further notice”, adding radar and communications equipment was damaged and runways needed to be assessed. Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath. “People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP . “Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood.” The attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said. The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport, while Australia urged its citizens on Sunday to stay indoors altogether and “shelter in place”. The Houthis also claimed to have targeted the Dammam airport, whose official website on Sunday showed many flights — both departures and arrivals — were delayed. ‘Rewrite the rules’ Saturday’s airport strike, on the eve of Saudi Arabia’s high-profile convention and entertainment season, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing. With the summer heat subsiding, October also usually marks the beginning of the high season for Umrah pilgrims, with millions of Muslims from across the world flocking to Makkah. Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa. Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to rewrite the rules of the game”. “They want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them,” he said. “So if their airport in Sanaa has to be closed because of the Saudi air embargo, they want to do the same thing to Saudi Arabia.” On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said on Saturday. The Houthis claimed to have repelled them. Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

Centrafrique : la Télévision centrafricaine se dote d’un nouveau studio pour mieux «porter la voix de la République»
items.description: La Television centrafricaine s'est dotee d'un nouveau studio moderne, baptise « la 7ᵉ Republique », dont l'inauguration a ete effectuee le 9 octobre lors d'une ceremonie presidee par le Premier ministre, Felix Moloua, avec la presence de plusieurs membres du gouvernement, dont le ministre de l'Urbanisme, Hassane Bouba Ali, et le ministre d'etat a la Communication, le Dr Evariste Ngamana, maître d'œuvre du projet, selon la presse locale. « Aujourd'hui, nous ne receptionnons pas seulement un studio. Nous posons un acte de souverainete. La communication gouvernementale est le pilier de la transparence et de la bonne gouvernance. On ne peut pas parler de 7ᵉ Republique avec des outils de la 1ʳᵉ Republique », a declare le Dr Evariste Ngamana. Les medias publics comme instrument « d'information, d'education, de culture et de cohesion nationale » Le ministre de la Communication centrafricain a fait part de la volonte du gouvernement de faire de ses medias publics de « veritables instruments d'information, d'education, de culture et de cohesion nationale ». Dans ce contexte, il a explique : « Nous ne pouvons pas demander a nos medias publics de porter la voix de la Republique, d'accompagner les transformations de notre pays et de repondre aux exigences du numerique avec des outils qui appartiennent parfois a une autre epoque. » « Notre ambition est de faire mieux, de produire davantage de contenus de qualite, d'etre plus proches des citoyens », a-t-il souligne. Projet concretise grâce au partenariat public-prive D'apres le Dr Evariste Ngamana, la vetuste des equipements dont dispose la tele nationale avait rendu necessaire la recherche de nouvelles solutions. C'est dans ce cadre que le projet a ete mis sur pied grâce a un partenariat public-prive, mettant a profit l'expertise de l'entreprise Descom, qui a finance la rehabilitation du studio. Des investissements ont egalement ete consacres a l'autonomie energetique des stations dans le but de limiter les interruptions d'antenne causees par les coupures d'electricite, selon le ministre. Des l'inauguration du studio, cette nouvelle structure a accueilli un grand debat diffuse en direct par la Television centrafricaine, durant lequel les ministres presents se sont succedes sur le plateau pour defendre leur bilan et repondre aux questions des journalistes et des telespectateurs.

items.title: Umahi defends Ondo Coastal Highway diversion
items.description: …Minister cites 100-metre-deep pits, high construction costs behind route change By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Works, David Umahi, has defended the Federal Government’s decision to divert the Ondo section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, saying the original route crossed terrain with pits more than 100 metres deep and would have significantly increased construction costs. Umahi spoke in Abuja while providing an update on President Bola Tinubu’s four legacy road projects, insisting that the diversion was based on engineering considerations and the need to ensure value for public funds. The minister said he was aware of petitions accusing him of diverting the route in Ondo State but maintained that the decision was justified. “I am aware of petitions against me saying I diverted the Ondo section. I welcome that. That is how it is supposed to be because we are serving the public. You are subject to public scrutiny. “But the important thing is whether you are doing the right thing or the wrong thing. We have no regret for decisions taken in Ondo,” he said. According to Umahi, the original alignment passed through terrain with pits exceeding 100 metres in depth and lacked suitable sharp sand for up to 300 metres, making construction along the corridor considerably more expensive. “You want me to pass through a terrain that you have over 100 metres of pits deep, and I have no defined sharp sand to 300 metres, and you expect the cost of one kilometre to be the same cost with a road passing through normal terrain?” he asked. He said the ministry consequently undertook a detour and redesign to avoid the difficult terrain. “We had to take a very serious engineering decision by making a detour, redesigning it to avoid such route. We are doing filling of over 10 metres, which is 30 feet plus, with sharp sand, and filling is almost concluded,” the minister said. The diversion affects Sections 4A and 4B of the coastal highway, covering 67 kilometres, comprising 27 kilometres in Ogun State and about 40 kilometres in Ondo State. The section will terminate around the Ondo-Edo axis. Progress on coastal highway Providing an update on the wider project, Umahi said Section 1, a 47.47-kilometre stretch from Victoria Island, Lagos, had been completed and was ready for commissioning. He added that the dual pavement on Section 2, which covers 55 kilometres and terminates at the Lagos-Ogun boundary, would be completed next month. The minister said the flyovers, overpasses and underpasses on Section 2 had required extensive redesign, particularly around the Dangote Refinery and Lekki Deep Seaport. He explained that an 86-metre-span bridge, with 43-metre counterforts, had been designed to accommodate refinery trucks and resolve a traffic conflict involving the deep-seaport train, the Dangote tax-credit road and the 25-kilometre Seventh Axial Road linking Epe to the Sagamu Expressway. “We have redesigned a very beautiful flyover to resolve that conflict,” Umahi said. At the Calabar end, he said Sections 3A and 3B, covering 65 kilometres, had achieved more than 30 per cent completion. He added that work was ongoing on Section 5, an 82-kilometre dual carriageway in Akwa Ibom State, alongside an 88-kilometre link from Calabar to Ebidi Beach intended to connect with the Trans-Saharan route. East-West Road alignment Umahi also disclosed that Tinubu had directed that the continuation of the coastal highway from Ondo into Edo State should follow the existing East-West Road rather than a new alignment. Describing the directive as a major development, the minister said the existing road had been constructed without adequate consideration for climate change and rising flood risks. He cited flooding at Ahoada about two weeks earlier, saying the permanent solution would involve raising sections of the road to protect it from current and projected flood levels. “The permanent solution is the decision of Mr President to align the continuation through the East-West Road. We now have to raise the road in many locations by two metres to be above present and expected flood levels,” he said. He put the Ondo-Edo corridor at 104 kilometres, including the 45-kilometre Benin Bypass, which he said would eliminate the need for motorists to pass through Benin City’s urban centre and help ease persistent traffic congestion. “That is the only solution whereby you don’t have to pass through the urban centre of Benin City. This decision is going to boost the economy,” he said, commending the governors of Edo and Delta states for supporting federal road projects. Other Niger Delta road projects The minister said the 129-kilometre dual carriageway from the Edo-Delta boundary to the Delta-Bayelsa boundary was undergoing route surveys and procurement, with construction expected to begin in November. He also said work was ongoing on the 15-kilometre Eleme Junction-to-Onne section and the 9.7-kilometre Eket Bypass. On the road linking Akwa Ibom to Calabar through Odukpani, Umahi said Hitech and Sammya Tech had been mobilised for emergency palliative works and full reconstruction of the 82-kilometre dualised stretch. He explained that the CCECC contract had been descoped because of funding challenges. Umahi urged residents of the Niger Delta to recognise the Federal Government’s interventions in road infrastructure across the region. “That is the story about the first legacy project of Mr President, and the people of the Niger Delta need to commend the President very, very highly,” he said. The post Umahi defends Ondo Coastal Highway diversion appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: A Spot-On SNL Parody About Men Who Can’t Deal With Time’s Passage
items.description: Even if you don’t know much country music, you likely know how much the genre loves the trope of the weepy father at his daughter’s wedding. In the best sketch of last night’s Saturday Night Live , the father of the bride was played by the host, Shane Gillis, but he wasn’t reflecting on life’s heavy milestones. Instead, he was thinking about “all the cool shit I can put in her room.” As narrated by a Rascal Flatts–esque band (composed of Andrew Dismukes, James Austin Johnson, and Tommy Brennan), the dad imagined everything he was going to put in his new man cave: a Ms. Pac-Man machine and a pinball machine; a drum set that he swore he would finally learn to play; a life-size cutout of Shaquille O’Neal; a bottle of lotion and box of tissues (a bit stolen from the Paul Rudd film I Love You, Man); a House box set; a cotton-candy machine. A child’s wedding is a joyous occasion, a new chapter for the family. But any beginning also reminds us that time’s arrow stubbornly points in only one direction. The sketch smartly underscored how many American men use consumer goods to distract themselves from anxieties about aging and the creeping sense that life may pass them by. Why deal with your uneasy feelings when you can finally afford the replica of a Star Wars stormtrooper you’ve wanted—nay, deserved—since you were a teenager? The hit of dopamine from a shopping spree is certainly more fun than wrestling with where your life currently stands. The best SNL song sketches expand on a central idea as the parody progresses, commenting on the characters’ comedic dilemmas. They also need to nail the musical references (Tim McGraw, Alan Jackson, Zac Brown, and, yes, Rascal Flatts have all released songs on this theme, something that the southerners Dismukes and Johnson are likely aware of). In last night’s sketch, we learned that Gillis’s presumably long-suffering wife (Ashley Padilla) “hates my room / we’re drifting apart,” and that she’s becoming a bit too close with her Zumba instructor, Tad (Marcello Hernández), “who’s actually pretty cool”—an off-hand remark from a man too clueless to see what’s coming next. Whatever you think about him, last night’s host was well equipped for this exploration of male obliviousness. [ Read: What Shane Gillis proved on SNL ] In 2019, Gillis was set to join SNL before some of his old offensive jokes resurfaced and NBC rescinded the offer . Gillis apologized for the material, and SNL ’s creator, Lorne Michaels, indicated that the casting decision was out of his hands . Michaels seems to have some lingering regrets about how it all went down; last night was Gillis’s third time hosting. But this overcorrection is arguably not doing Gillis many favors, as the episode often demonstrated his limitations as a comedian . He flubbed most of his lines—and cursed—in a sketch parodying Green Eggs and Ham , then apologized “about earlier” during the episode’s closing goodbyes. Gillis tends to embody characters who aren’t actively hateful or toxic but just a little confused about society’s changing social mores and unsure about what they’re allowed to say. But Gillis, who lacks the dexterity of clear influences such as Louis C.K. and Dave Chappelle, can’t consistently pull off that tricky balance of thoughtfulness and provocation. During his opening monologue, in a bit about struggling to seem nonthreatening when he encounters a woman on an otherwise solitary hike, he lost the audience after saying, “I haven’t been to the gym in so long I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?” (I’ll spare you his description of women’s modern athleisure wear.) By that point, the crowd was so cold he couldn’t win it back with a clever closing riff about society’s polarization and the dangers of ambiguous haircuts: “You’re either gay or you’re Hitler, and isn’t that where we’re at as a country?” Still, Gillis has become a successful touring comedian, mostly because he is very good at expressing the immaturity, simmering hostility, and general dunderheadedness of a certain strain of American manhood. His best sketches from last night made use of that meathead persona, as when he played a jerky police officer hosting the discussion show Cop Talk and the manager of an HVAC company that prided itself on having the most off-putting employees you would ever encounter. But the wedding-song sketch stood out because it zeroed in on the stunted emotional life of Gillis’s character and then mocked it relentlessly. After his wife left him for Tad, he decided to build an even bigger room of one’s own (“Super Room Rocks!”), but when the impromptu construction project exposed him to black mold, he began “tripping balls.” The story eventually took an unexpectedly frisky turn before the episode’s kicker revealed this entire misadventure was a dream sequence that began after he forgot to help his daughter and wife pack up the moving van—a sly commentary on the character’s misplaced priorities. It’s hard to say whether Gillis found success because he’s secretly very perceptive about the state of modern masculinity or because he’s unafraid to admit just how unperceptive he is about the modern world. Either way, last night’s song fulfilled the country-music imperative of “three chords and the truth”: a catchy ballad about how many men are emotionally stunted and unable to deal with aging and change, and will instead retreat into materialism and adolescent interests rather than reconcile with life’s relentless momentum.

items.title: CNG transport cuts commuters’ fares, saves money – Tinubu
items.description: President cites lower fares, new buses, tax waivers to ease transport costs By Nwafor Sunday, Online News Editor President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has said investments in compressed natural gas (CNG) transportation are helping to reduce transport fares and ease the financial burden on Nigerians amid rising petrol prices. Tinubu disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, citing accounts from commuters and commercial drivers who said they were spending less on transportation after switching to CNG-powered and electric vehicles. Addressing a commuter identified as Blessing, the President said her journey from Masaka to Berger in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) now cost ₦500, down from ₦1,500, saving her ₦1,000 per trip. He also cited the experiences of Ada and Abigail, who reportedly now pay ₦1,600 instead of ₦4,000 to travel from Enugu to Nsukka, saving ₦2,400 per journey. Tinubu said a taxi driver, Kabir, had reported that spending ₦10,000 on CNG enabled him to make three more return trips than colleagues using petrol. The President added that he had received encouraging feedback from Borno State, where some commuters reportedly paid as little as ₦50 per trip on CNG-powered and electric vehicles. According to him, the experiences demonstrate the intended benefits of government investment in alternative-fuel transportation. “Lower operating costs for drivers should translate into more affordable fares for passengers, leaving families with more money for their everyday needs,” he said. Tinubu acknowledged that the removal of the petrol subsidy had created difficulties for many households, but said the decision also placed a responsibility on his administration to provide practical alternatives to reduce transportation costs. He said the government was working with state governments, through the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, and private investors to expand affordable transport services under the National Affordable CNG Transportation Programme. More buses, electric vehicles Responding to a request for more buses from a Nigerian identified as Emmanuel, Tinubu said his administration was working to extend affordable transportation services to more communities. He disclosed that Ekiti State had received 15 buses in recent weeks, while Lagos received 20 and Akwa Ibom had 50 buses ready for service. According to the President, Katsina State had introduced 30 CNG hybrid buses and 200 electric tricycles, while Kano had received 30 CNG buses and five electric buses. He added that another rollout was scheduled for Edo State. Tinubu also said Kaduna’s 100 CNG buses had transported more than three million passengers to date. Beyond public transport, he disclosed that more than 400 certified centres had converted over 120,000 vehicles to CNG, while the government was expanding refuelling infrastructure to improve access to the fuel. Government announces relief measures The President also acknowledged the pressure rising petrol prices were placing on households and businesses, outlining measures his administration said were aimed at cushioning the impact. He said the government had waived more than ₦3.3 trillion in fuel taxes and duties. Tinubu further disclosed that NNPC Retail was foregoing its profit margin for 30 days, with priority given to public transport operators. He added that the government was working towards a ceiling of ₦1,350 per litre on wholesale petrol supply costs to reduce price volatility. “These measures are intended to ease the immediate burden while we continue expanding affordable transportation alternatives,” the President said. The post CNG transport cuts commuters’ fares, saves money – Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina: « Près de 350 000 personnes ont eu accès aux soins de santé » grâce au CICR
items.description: La Délégation du Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) au Burkina Faso, a organisé un café-presse, le vendredi 9 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou pour faire le point de ses interventions et annoncer la commémoration des 20 ans d'existence physique de la structure dans le pays. Au cours du premier semestre, les actions du CICR ont permis à « près de 350 000 personnes d'avoir accès aux soins de santé », a déclaré Paguindama Emeline Yaméogo/Oboulbiga, coordinatrice communication et prévention du CICR au Burkina Faso. L'équipe du Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) a échangé, le vendredi 9 octobre 2026, avec les hommes et femmes de médias. Au cours de ces échanges, plusieurs responsables des équipes techniques opérant sur le terrain, ont montré l'impact des interventions de l'institution au bénéfice des populations burkinabè. Leur communication a plus concerné le bilan des actions menées au cours du premier semestre 2026 en faveur des communautés affectées et les activités commémoratives des 20 ans de l'intervention du CICR au Burkina Faso. Le chef de la délégation du CICR échangeant avec les journalistes « Nous avons tenu à échanger avec les médias pour justement présenter le bilan ou l'impact effectivement des activités que nous avons menées au premier semestre 2026 pour démontrer un peu comment ça a pu améliorer le quotidien des communautés affectées et comment cela a, également, été mis en œuvre avec le soutien des services techniques et étatiques ainsi que de tous les acteurs concernés », a déclaré la coordinatrice communication et prévention du CICR au Burkina Faso, Paguindama Emeline Yaméogo/Oboulbiga, poursuivant que cette rencontre visait aussi à annoncer les perspectives de l'Institution pour le second semestre. Sur le bilan du premier semestre, « il y a près de 350 000 personnes qui ont eu accès aux soins de santé, qu'ils soient curatifs ou préventifs. Il y a près de 69 000 ménages qui ont reçu une assistance d'urgence en vivres. Il y a aussi près de 20 000 ménages qui ont également reçu une assistance en semences pour leur permettre de pouvoir développer leur culture maraîchère. Donc tout ceci nous amène à dire que ces actions, aussi minimes soient-elles, en tout cas, ont pu contribuer quand même à renforcer l'autonomie et la résilience des populations que nous avons aidées », a-t-elle soutenu. Emeline Yaméogo/Oboulbiga, coordinatrice Prévention et Communication du CICR Vu les actions égrenées, le CICR « est satisfait » au regard de ses réalités, de ses priorités opérationnelles, de ses défis auxquels il est confrontés, s'est réjouie la coordinatrice communication et prévention de l'institution qui pense que le CICR a pu répondre à son niveau, aux besoins qu'il a pu observer. « Et nous pensons que c'est une contribution à l'ensemble des actions que d'autres acteurs et surtout le gouvernement également mettent en œuvre », a-t-elle laissé entendre, rassurant de la poursuite des efforts dans ce sens pour continuer à travailler avec les communautés à pouvoir poser des actions en vue de leur permettre d'être encore plus résilientes. Sur l'anniversaire des 20 ans de présence effective du CICR au Burkina Faso depuis février 2006, les interlocuteurs des journalistes à ce café de presse ont invité leurs partenaires à prendre part activement à la commémoration pour l'épanouissement des populations. « Il faut dire que ces 20 ans de présence permanente ne peuvent pas aussi occulter 30 ans d'engagement que le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge a eu aux côtés du Burkina Faso, notamment, en travaillant avec la Croix-Rouge Burkinabè, les autorités, les communautés et les différents acteurs dans le cadre de son mandat exclusivement humanitaire qui est de protéger la vie et la dignité des personnes affectées ou vulnérables que ce soit par des situations de conflits ou de violences », a-t-elle expliqué. Cette période de commémoration qui aura lieu vers fin octobre – début novembre sera une halte pour permettre à l'institution de regarder ce qui a été fait durant ces 20 dernières années pour saluer toutes les personnes qui ont contribué à ses actions pour également encourager davantage les communautés et surtout réitérer l'engagement indéfectible du CICR à poursuivre sa mission humanitaire, selon ses priorités et les besoins des communautés. « Idéalement, on va faire une commémoration assez sobre, vraiment orientée sur la réflexion, la projection d'un CICR qui se veut plus proche, plus pertinent et plus efficace », a soutenu, dans ce sens, Mme Emeline Yaméogo, annonçant une campagne digitale qui va mettre en lumière des portraits des personnes qui ont jalonné ces 20 ans de présence de la structure et un film documentaire qui sera réalisé pour retracer un peu l'effet majeur de ces 20 ans. Le.Chef de la délégation du CICR, Yves Arnoldy Le CICR prévoit organiser aussi une soirée de commémoration pour réunir autour d'une même table différents acteurs: autorités étatiques, acteurs académiques, mondes diplomatiques, communautés partenaires et médias pour faire le point de ces 20 ans, tirer les leçons et aussi se projeter pour les années à venir en réitérant l'engagement humanitaire que l'institution veut toujours plus grand au Burkina. En rappel, au Burkina Faso, le CICR intervient dans les domaines de la ne protection, de la prévention/communication, de l'assistance, de la sécurité alimentaire et de la coopération. Par Bernard BOUGOUM L’article Burkina: « Près de 350 000 personnes ont eu accès aux soins de santé » grâce au CICR est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Maaz Sadaqat, Imran Randhawa star as Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka in second T20I to seal series
items.description: Maaz Sadaqat hit a blistering 96 before Imran Randhawa’s miserly spell helped Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second Twenty20 International and seal the three-match series for the hosts here at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Both Maaz and Imran were able to make a match-winning impact in what was only their second T20I outing after making their debuts in Friday’s opening match. While Maaz — who had hit a crucial half-century on debut — went on to showcase the more belligerent side of his potential, Imran justified his selection with precision bowling that kept Sri Lanka from getting into the game at any point during the chase. After Pakistan were restricted to 46 in the powerplay, Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz transformed the innings with a commanding 88-run partnership for the second wicket. Farhan, who survived a couple of reprieves, led the recovery with a fluent 73 off 44 balls, striking four fours and five sixes, while Maaz provided the acceleration that ultimately carried Pakistan to their highest T20I total on home soil. Fakhar Zaman had contributed 22 off 17 balls before falling to Maheesh Theekshana in the seventh over, but Maaz initially took time to settle after his arrival. He survived a leading edge that fell short of cover and was dropped by Nuwan Thushara off his own bowling on 44, before making Sri Lanka pay dearly for their lapses. The left-hander brought up his half-century off 29 balls with a towering six over long-off against Theekshana in the 15th over. What followed was a remarkable exhibition of power-hitting as Maaz plundered 22 runs from the spinner’s final over, striking three sixes to take Pakistan past 165. He continued to dismantle the bowling attack, using his feet against the pacers and finding boundaries on both sides of the wicket. His audacious scoop, reverse paddle and clean strikes over the ropes left Sri Lanka struggling for answers as Pakistan surged towards 200. Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat convene during their partnership during the second Twenty20 International against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 11, 2026.—AFP Farhan, meanwhile, brought up his half-century off 32 balls and continued to attack before Dasun Shanaka finally dismissed him in the 15th over, caught at deep third for 73. Maaz then took charge alongside Hasan Nawaz, who struck an unbeaten 19 off nine deliveries, as Pakistan collected 49 runs across the final three overs before the last. Maaz reached 96 off just 51 balls, with six fours and seven sixes, but his maiden T20I century remained agonisingly out of reach. Attempting to slice Eshan Malinga behind point off the final delivery, he found Shanaka at deep cover instead. Pakistan nevertheless finished on 215-3, setting Sri Lanka a daunting target of 216. Sri Lanka’s reply unravelled almost immediately. Salman Mirza, returning to international cricket after injury, removed Lahiru Udara for five in the opening over, before Imran struck to dismiss Sineth Jayawardena for 22 at the end of the powerplay. Imran then delivered the decisive blows in the eighth over, removing captain Kusal Mendis for nine and Sahan Arachchige for a duck off successive deliveries, with wicket-keeper Khawaja Nafay taking two sharp catches. His figures improved to 3-9 after three overs, leaving Sri Lanka reeling at 49-4. The 29-year-old completed an outstanding spell of four overs for just 11 runs and three wickets, conceding only five runs in his first two overs. Dasun Shanaka fell to Saim Ayub for nine, while Shadab Khan dismissed Kamindu Mendis for 23 to leave the visitors at 74-6. Chamindu Wickramasinghe and Maheesh Theekshana offered some resistance with a seventh-wicket stand of 50, but the required rate had climbed beyond reach. Chamindu made 29 before falling to Salman Mirza, who finished with two wickets, while Theekshana remained unbeaten on 32 off 26 balls. Pakistan’s Imran Randhawa (L) and Fakhar Zaman (R) celebrate during the second Twenty20 International against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 11, 2026.—AFP Sri Lanka closed on 133-7, handing Pakistan an emphatic 82-run victory and an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series ahead of Tuesday’s final match. Farhan, celebrating his first series victory as Pakistan captain, praised his side’s improved six-hitting and attacking intent, while Sri Lanka skipper Mendis admitted his batters needed to take greater responsibility on a surface suited to stroke-making. Maaz was named player of the match for his explosive innings, but Imran’s disciplined spell ensured that Pakistan’s outstanding batting display translated into a series-clinching victory.

items.title: Man City thrash Liverpool 3-0 amid financial charges, extend lead at top
items.description: Manchester City shrugged off the threat of swingeing sanctions to beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 in their first game since being found guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules. Second half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki extended City’s flawless start under Enzo Maresca after Ryan Gravenberch had been sent-off for two yellow cards. Victory reestablishes City’s three-point lead at the top of the table, but the future of any title challenge rests on the outcome of the club’s appeal against widespread financial impropriety. An independent commission found City and their Emirati owners arranged “sham” deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018. No sanction has yet been handed down, but a severe points deduction or even expulsion from the English top-flight are on the table unless City overturn the decision. There has even been speculation there could be retrospective action to strip titles. The multiple breaches of Premier League laws came during a period in which City won three titles and a clutch of other trophies. City’s rivals believe, however, that the illegal spending during that period also built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who left at the end of last season. Liverpool were one of the clubs most affected, having finished second to City three times in the past 12 years. “There are so many moments and memories we can’t get back,” Liverpool fan Martin Reilly, 23, told AFP. “They have to throw the book at them.” City arrived under the protection of a police escort with a hostile Anfield welcome expected, but there was no repeat of the violent scenes when their team bus was pelted by bottles ahead of a Champions League clash in 2018. Liverpool fans lined the streets to greet the visitors with chants of “cheats” and “going down”, while merchandise stalls were littered with flags and scarves mocking City’s financial scandal. In the iconic Kop end behind one goal a banner read “a generation of supporters cheated.” The battles between Guardiola’s City and Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool in recent years became the Premier League’s marquee event. But with the eyes of the world watching, Liverpool failed to rise to the occasion on the field. New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola’s options were blunted without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo as the Spaniard suffered his first defeat since taking charge of the Reds. The home side briefly flickered into life at the start of the second half when Lewis Koumas was denied a goal on his first Premier League start by Gianluigi Donnarumma. An Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008 transformed City from mid-table mediocrity into the dominant force of the English game. City’s economic might was in full show help turn the game as Maresca could turn to Jeremy Doku off the bench early in the second half. Within minutes the Belgian winger had been chopped down by Gravenberch, who was shown a harsh second booking and Liverpool never recovered. Doku’s deflected shot was then smashed home by Haaland to break the deadlock 25 minutes from time and open the floodgates. Three minutes later Doku curled a sensational strike into the top corner himself. Cherki then exchanged a slick one-two with Josko Gvardiol before slotting under Alisson Becker to rub salt in Liverpool wounds. items.title: WAFU B U17: Ghana top Group A after win over Togo
items.description: The Black Starlets have moved to the top of Group A at the 2026 WAFU Zone B U-17 Championship following their 1-0 victory over Togo on Saturday in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. David Kwarteng scored the decisive goal in the seventh minute at the August 4 Sports Stadium to hand the Black Starlets all three points in their opening fixture of the competition, which serves as the qualifying tournament for the 2027 U-17 Africa Cup of Nations. The result puts Ghana in a strong position in Group A after hosts Burkina Faso and Benin played out a goalless draw in the other opening-day encounter. Ghana lead the group with three points, while Burkina Faso and Benin have one point each, with Togo yet to register a point. items.title: INEC lists 19 governorship candidates for Taraba
items.description: Agbu Kefas, Emmanuel Bwacha, Abubakar Tutare among contenders By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has published the final list of governorship and deputy-governorship candidates for the 2027 election in Taraba State, featuring contenders from 19 political parties. Among those listed is the incumbent governor, Agbu Kefas, who is the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), with Ibrahim Zainab Abubakar as his running mate. Former senator Emmanuel Bwacha is listed as the candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), while former federal lawmaker Danjuma Usman Shiddi will contest on the platform of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA). Other governorship candidates on the list include Prof. Jerome Nyameh of Accord; Gago Magaji Bulus of the African Action Congress (AAC); Hamman Abubakar Mustapha of the Action Democratic Party (ADP); Bawa Ishaka Mohammed of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM); and Henry Haniel Banti of the Action Peoples Party (APP). Also listed are Kabiru Bala of the Boot Party (BP); Aboki Boyonga Stephen of the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA); Yahaya Mohammed Sani of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC); Nuhu Abubakar Atta of the National Democratic Party (NDP); and Josiah Wukari Wasa of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP). The remaining candidates are Sa’ad Hassan Abubakar of the Young Progressives Party (YPP); Bello Adamu of the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP); Nathan Sanda of the Labour Party (LP); Uba Sani Abdullahi of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP); Yusuf Ali of the Social Democratic Party (SDP); and former senator Abubakar Umar Tutare of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The publication of the final list sets out the candidates cleared by INEC to contest the Taraba governorship election in 2027. items.title: SDP to engage INEC over omission of four guber candidates
items.description: Party explores 14-day window under Electoral Act 2026 to correct errors By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has said it will engage the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over the omission of its governorship candidates in Oyo, Bauchi, Benue and Sokoto states from the list of candidates for the 2027 elections. The party said it had commenced efforts to activate corrective measures, expressing confidence that the omissions would be addressed promptly by the electoral commission. The SDP said it was exploring the 14-day window provided under the Electoral Act 2026 to correct errors identified in INEC’s publication. Reacting to the development on Sunday, the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Araba Rufus Aiyenigba, said the omission of its governorship candidates in the four states, as well as some candidates contesting state constituency seats, had raised concerns among supporters in the affected areas. “Regrettably, SDP governorship candidates for four states were omitted — Benue, Oyo, Bauchi and Sokoto — and also some of our candidates in a number of state constituencies,” Aiyenigba said. “This unexpected error, undeniably, has elicited worries amongst our supporters in the states affected. “The affected candidates have been assured that the error is being addressed with the deserved seriousness, and there are high assurances that the corrections will be effected promptly by the commission. “The party has commenced the process of activating the corrective measures, exploring the 14-day window provision of the Electoral Act 2026 to correct errors noted in the publication.” Aiyenigba urged affected candidates to reassure their supporters that efforts were underway to resolve the issue, while encouraging them to sustain their campaign activities. Among those affected are the SDP governorship candidate in Benue State, Prof. Sebastine Hon, SAN, and the party’s candidate in Oyo State, Mogaji Olusegun Agboola, whose names were reportedly missing from the list released by INEC. The party said it remained committed to ensuring that the omissions were corrected through the appropriate process. items.title: Huile, viandes, café : le PLF 2027 propose de reconduire les subventions jusqu’en 2029
items.description: Dans un contexte d'efforts soutenus pour préserver le pouvoir d’achat, le Projet de loi de finances pour 2027 (PLF 2027) propose de reconduire de nombreuses mesures fiscales prises ces dernières années pour soutenir les prix de certains produits alimentaires de base. Le soutien s'inscrit dans la durée puisque la proposition faite dans le texte porte sur le maintien desdites mesures pour trois années supplémentaires, jusqu'au 31 décembre 2029. Viandes : les droits de douane réduits (5 %) maintenus Le gouvernement explique que la proposition vise à reconduire les mesures temporaires visant à garantir l’approvisionnement du marché en produits alimentaires de large consommation, comme les viandes rouges et blanches, les huiles alimentaires, le café, les légumes secs, le riz et les œufs. Il s'agit de préserver le pouvoir d’achat en maîtrisant les prix et constituer un stock de sécurité, “ tout en accompagnant les stratégies nationales de développement de la production locale ”. Pour soutenir les prix de ces produits, les pouvoirs publics ont agi, dans la période 2023-2026, sur les droits de douanes et les exonérations fiscales. La satisfaction des besoins du marché national “ nécessite encore le recours à l’importation ” et, “ pour combler le déficit constaté ” pour les produits en question, il est proposé de proroger jusqu’au 31 décembre 2029 plusieurs dispositions de soutien aux prix prises ces dernières années. TVA et TIC suspendues sur de nombreux produits jusqu'en 2029 Il s'agit notamment des dispositions des article 139 et 140 de la Loi de finances pour 2026, prévoyant l’application d’un taux réduit (5 %) de droits de douane aux importations de cheptels bovins et ovins vivants destinés à l’abattage, aux viandes bovines et ovines fraîches réfrigérées sous vide (une mesure étendue à certaines catégories de bovins vivants destinés à l’engraissement), et aux opérations d’importation de viandes blanches congelées. Le PLF 2027 propose aussi de proroger pour la même durée les stipulations de l’article 214 de la Loi de finances pour 2025 portant exonération de la TVA et de la taxe intérieure de consommation (TIC) des opérations d’importation de café vert, ainsi que celles de l’article 65 de la Loi de finances pour 2024, exonérant de la TVA les importations et la vente de riz, pois, pois chiches, haricots, lentilles, fèves et autres légumes secs à cosse et aussi les opérations de vente de fruits et légumes frais, d’œufs de consommation, de poulet de chair et de dinde produits localement. Délai prorogé pour les transformateurs d’huile de soja S'agissant des huiles de table, le PLF 2027 propose de reconduire la mesure contenue dans la LF 2022 relative à l’exonération de la TVA de l’huile brute et des tourteaux issus de la trituration locale des graines oléagineuses, ainsi que celle, contenue dans la même LF 2022, fixant un délai à partir duquel les importateurs et transformateurs locaux pourront continuer à bénéficier des mécanismes de compensation des prix de l’huile brute de soja importée et des exonérations douanières et fiscales lorsque l’huile brute n’est pas disponible sur le marché national. Prorogée à chaque fois d’une année par les différentes lois de finances ces dernières années, le PLF 2027 propose de maintenir la mesure jusqu’en 2029. Il est stipulé que “ les importateurs/transformateurs de l’huile brute de soja sont tenus, soit d’entamer le processus de production de cette matière première, soit de l’acquérir sur le marché national, au plus tard, le 31 décembre 2029 ”. L’article Huile, viandes, café : le PLF 2027 propose de reconduire les subventions jusqu'en 2029 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Promotion du Basketball à Ziguinchor : la coupe du maire reprend ses droits
items.description: Neuf équipes masculines et quatre formations féminines sont en lice pour la deuxième édition de la coupe du maire de basket-ball, officiellement lancée samedi 10 octobre à Ziguinchor. Au-delà de la bataille sur les parquets, la compétition ambitionne de donner du rythme aux clubs, révéler les talents et faire des infrastructures sportives un levier d’épanouissement et de développement local. Dans la capitale régionale du sud, le basket-ball entend désormais gagner du terrain, sur les parquets comme dans la vie des quartiers. Avec le lancement de la deuxième édition de la coupe du maire, la municipalité remet les jeunes au cœur du jeu, en misant sur la compétition pour entretenir les talents, renforcer les clubs et donner une nouvelle impulsion au sport local. Pour le maire Djibril Sonko, l’enjeu dépasse les paniers marqués et les trophées à décrocher. « Avec cette compétition, nous voulons animer la ville le week-end et créer une activité économique autour des rencontres », a indiqué le successeur d’Ousmane Sonko. Lors des matchs, les vendeurs de cacahuètes et petits commerçants vont profiter de l’affluence, dans une dynamique que l’édile souhaite étendre au football dès novembre, avec une compétition destinée aux clubs affiliés à la Fédération sénégalaise de football. Sur le terrain, le maire de la commune de Ziguinchor a affirmé que la coupe doit également servir de préparation aux équipes locales avant les échéances nationales. « J'invite les joueurs à prendre ce rendez-vous au sérieux, convaincu que la multiplication des rencontres est indispensable à leur progression technique et physique », a insisté Djibril Sonko. Mais cette ambition se heurte à un défi majeur : la disponibilité d’infrastructures adaptées. Sur ce aspect precis, Djibril Sonko a annoncé la prochaine réhabilitation du stade Jules-François-Bocandé, avec la pose d’une pelouse synthétique. Pour le basket-ball, il a précisé que des discussions sont en cours avec la Ligue régionale afin « d’améliorer les terrains de la commune et de couvrir celui du stade, pour permettre aux joueurs d’évoluer dans de meilleures conditions ». Pour sa part, le président de la Ligue régionale, Mamadou Lamine Saul Sidibé, a salué une initiative qu’il juge remarquable dans le paysage sportif local. Selon lui, l’organisation d’une cérémonie officielle de lancement « constitue un signal fort pour une discipline qui a contribué à révéler de nombreux talents sénégalais ». Avec treize équipes engagées, cette deuxième édition place ainsi le basket-ball au croisement de plusieurs enjeux liés à la formation des jeunes, à la compétitivité des clubs, à l’animation économique et à la modernisation des équipements. À Ziguinchor, le coup d’envoi est donné. Il reste à transformer cette dynamique en opportunités durables pour la jeunesse. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)
